items.name: Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage Inc.
items.label: Reported results

performance.driver: Net sales for fiscal 2026 in the Aerospace/Defense sector increased $158.3 million, or 23.0%, as compared to fiscal 2025. The increase in net sales was driven by overall net increased customer end-market demand, an increase of $44.9 million due to production ramps of new products for existing customers and an increase of $31.1 million due to production ramps for new customers.

Net Sales Net sales decreased $38.1 million, or less than 1%, during the year ended September 30, 2026, when compared to the prior year, driven by lower net sales within our Refrigerated Retail and Foodservice segments, partially offset by higher net sales within our Post Consumer Brands and Weetabix segments.

Operating income Our operating income increased by $483 million to $1,177 million for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 from $694 million for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025. The increase in operating income was due to the same factors affecting Adjusted OIBDA above, partially offset by higher amortization expenses of $25 million and higher depreciation expenses of $9 million, as noted above.

Operating Profit Operating profit decreased $79.7 million, or 22%, during the year ended September 30, 2026 compared to the prior year. This decrease was primarily driven by higher net product costs of $135.8 million, increased advertising expenses of $16.0 million, and $5.9 million of reorganization charges, and was partially offset by a $69.0 million provision in legal matters in the prior year.

Operating Income $ 11,191 $ 9,995 12 % Revenues - Theme park admissions The increase in theme park admissions revenue was due to increases of 5% from higher average per capita ticket revenue, 2% from the additional week of operations and 1% from increased attendance.

performance.driver: Revenue decreased $145.3 million, or 6.3%, to approximately $2.164 billion for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 from $2.309 billion for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025. The decrease is due to a $125.2 million or 6% decrease in comparable-store sales, in addition to a $20.1 million net decrease from closed stores and manufacturing revenue that are not eligible for inclusion in comparable-store sales.
